definitions.simple: Blood pressure that stays higher than the healthy range.
definitions.standard: Persistently elevated pressure of blood against artery walls.
definitions.technical: A clinical condition of sustained elevation in arterial blood pressure, assessed through repeated measurements.

examples: Hypertension is the medical term for high blood pressure.

definitions.simple: Blood pressure that is lower than expected.
definitions.standard: Abnormally low arterial blood pressure, which may or may not cause symptoms.
definitions.technical: A reduction in systemic arterial pressure below the range expected for the clinical context.

examples: Dizziness can occur with hypotension, but the word itself is not a diagnosis of the cause.

definitions.simple: A heart rate that is faster than expected.
definitions.standard: A faster-than-normal heart rate for the person's age and situation.
definitions.technical: An elevated heart rate relative to the expected physiologic range and clinical context.

examples: Tachycardia describes a fast heart rate; it does not identify the cause by itself.

definitions.simple: A heart rate that is slower than expected.
definitions.standard: A slower-than-normal heart rate for the person's age and situation.
definitions.technical: A heart rate below the expected physiologic range in its clinical context.

examples: Bradycardia describes a slow heart rate but does not identify its cause.

definitions.simple: A lower-than-normal level of glucose in the blood.
definitions.standard: A condition in which blood glucose falls below the expected range.
definitions.technical: A biochemical state of reduced circulating glucose; clinically meaningful thresholds depend on context.

examples: Hypoglycemia means that blood glucose is below its expected range.

definitions.simple: A higher-than-normal level of glucose in the blood.
definitions.standard: A condition in which blood glucose is above the expected range.
definitions.technical: A biochemical state of elevated circulating glucose; interpretation depends on timing and clinical context.

examples: Hyperglycemia means that blood glucose is above its expected range.

definitions.simple: Inflammation involving the stomach and intestines.
definitions.standard: Inflammation of the stomach and intestinal tract, often associated with digestive symptoms.
definitions.technical: An inflammatory disorder involving the gastric and intestinal mucosa; the term does not specify a cause.

examples: The morphology explains the structures involved, while the sourced definition establishes the medical meaning.

definitions.simple: An operation to remove all or part of a kidney.
definitions.standard: Surgical removal of a kidney or a portion of a kidney.
definitions.technical: A surgical procedure involving partial or complete excision of renal tissue.

examples: Nephrectomy is the name of a surgical procedure, not a recommendation for treatment.

definitions.simple: Inflammation of the skin.
definitions.standard: A general term for inflammation of the skin, often with irritation or rash.
definitions.technical: Inflammation of cutaneous tissue; the term includes multiple conditions and does not specify cause.

examples: Dermatitis is a broad term and may have different causes.

definitions.simple: An enlarged liver.
definitions.standard: Enlargement of the liver beyond its expected size.
definitions.technical: Abnormal enlargement of the liver identified clinically or by imaging; the term does not state the cause.

examples: Hepatomegaly describes liver enlargement but not why it occurred.

definitions.simple: A disease affecting the heart muscle.
definitions.standard: A group of disorders in which the heart muscle is structurally or functionally abnormal.
definitions.technical: A heterogeneous group of myocardial disorders associated with mechanical or electrical dysfunction.

examples: Cardiomyopathy refers to heart muscle disease; specific types require clinical evaluation.

definitions.simple: A heart attack caused by loss of blood flow to part of the heart muscle.
definitions.standard: Injury and death of heart muscle tissue caused by prolonged interruption of its blood supply.
definitions.technical: Myocardial necrosis resulting from sustained ischemia, diagnosed using clinical criteria.

examples: Myocardial infarction is the medical term commonly associated with a heart attack.

definitions.simple: A feeling of difficult or uncomfortable breathing.
definitions.standard: The subjective experience of breathing discomfort or shortness of breath.
definitions.technical: A subjective sensation of breathing discomfort with varied qualitative characteristics and causes.

examples: Dyspnea describes the sensation and does not identify its cause.

definitions.simple: Swelling caused by fluid collecting in body tissues.
definitions.standard: Accumulation of excess fluid in tissue spaces, producing swelling.
definitions.technical: Abnormal expansion of interstitial fluid volume within tissues.

examples: Edema describes swelling from fluid accumulation but not the underlying cause.

definitions.simple: A condition in which the blood has too few healthy red blood cells or too little hemoglobin.
definitions.standard: Reduced red blood cell mass or hemoglobin concentration, limiting the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity.
definitions.technical: A reduction in circulating erythrocyte mass or hemoglobin below the reference range for the relevant population.

examples: Anemia is a broad finding with multiple possible causes.

definitions.simple: A long-term condition that affects the protective covering of nerves in the brain and spinal cord.
definitions.standard: A disorder of the central nervous system involving immune-mediated damage to myelin.
definitions.technical: A chronic inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system with variable neurologic manifestations.

examples: MS can mean multiple sclerosis in a neurologic context, but the abbreviation is ambiguous.

definitions.simple: Narrowing of the valve between the upper and lower chambers on the left side of the heart.
definitions.standard: Narrowing of the mitral valve opening that obstructs blood flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle.
definitions.technical: Obstruction of left ventricular inflow caused by narrowing of the mitral valve orifice.

examples: MS can mean mitral stenosis in a cardiology context, so context is required.

definitions.simple: The force of blood pushing against artery walls.
definitions.standard: The pressure produced as circulating blood pushes against blood-vessel walls.
definitions.technical: The pressure exerted by circulating blood on the walls of arteries, commonly expressed as systolic and diastolic values.

examples: BP commonly means blood pressure, but the surrounding context should still be checked.

definitions.simple: The number of heartbeats in a period of time, usually one minute.
definitions.standard: The frequency at which the heart beats, commonly measured in beats per minute.
definitions.technical: The frequency of cardiac cycles over time, conventionally recorded in beats per minute.

examples: HR commonly means heart rate in vital-sign documentation.

definitions.simple: An instruction not to eat or drink by mouth for a stated period.
definitions.standard: A clinical instruction to withhold oral food and fluids for a specified reason and duration.
definitions.technical: An order restricting oral intake; exact allowances and duration must be confirmed from the clinical team.

examples: NPO instructions require confirmation of timing and whether any medicines or fluids are permitted.

definitions.simple: Used only when needed within the instructions given.
definitions.standard: An instruction that an intervention may be used when a specified need occurs, within stated limits.
definitions.technical: A conditional administration instruction whose indication, amount, route, and maximum frequency must be specified elsewhere.

examples: PRN does not state the dose or maximum frequency; the complete instruction must be checked.

definitions.simple: Given through the mouth.
definitions.standard: Administration of a substance by mouth for swallowing.
definitions.technical: A route of administration in which a substance is taken through the mouth, generally for gastrointestinal absorption.

examples: PO commonly means by mouth; the complete instruction must still be read.

definitions.simple: Given into a vein.
definitions.standard: Administration directly into a vein through suitable vascular access.
definitions.technical: A parenteral route that introduces a substance into venous circulation.

examples: IV commonly refers to intravenous administration, but context must be confirmed.

definitions.simple: Given into a muscle.
definitions.standard: Administration by injection into muscle tissue.
definitions.technical: A parenteral route in which a substance is deposited within skeletal muscle.

examples: IM commonly means intramuscular, but the full instruction must be checked.

definitions.simple: Given into the tissue under the skin.
definitions.standard: Administration into subcutaneous tissue beneath the skin.
definitions.technical: A parenteral route in which a substance is deposited in the subcutaneous tissue.

examples: SC may mean subcutaneous in a medicine route, but context must be confirmed.

definitions.simple: Placed under the tongue.
definitions.standard: Administration beneath the tongue for local or systemic absorption.
definitions.technical: A route using the sublingual mucosa for absorption.

examples: SL may mean sublingual in a medicine route; check the complete instruction.

definitions.simple: One time in one day, according to the stated schedule.
definitions.standard: A frequency instruction indicating one administration per day; exact timing should be confirmed.
definitions.technical: A once-per-day dosing-frequency expression that does not itself specify clock time.

examples: OD may mean once daily or right eye, so context must be confirmed.

definitions.simple: At the person's usual bedtime, according to the complete instruction.
definitions.standard: A timing qualifier indicating administration at bedtime.
definitions.technical: A non-clock dosing-time qualifier whose exact time varies by person and instruction.

examples: HS may mean at bedtime or another clinical phrase; confirm context.

definitions.simple: Before eating, using the timing in the complete instruction.
definitions.standard: A meal-related timing qualifier indicating administration before meals.
definitions.technical: A preprandial administration qualifier that requires the full instruction for exact timing.

examples: AC can have other meanings, so check the prescription context.

definitions.simple: After eating, using the timing in the complete instruction.
definitions.standard: A meal-related timing qualifier indicating administration after meals.
definitions.technical: A postprandial administration qualifier that requires the full instruction for exact timing.

examples: PC can have other meanings, so check the prescription context.

definitions.simple: Without delay, according to the clinical instruction.
definitions.standard: An instruction indicating immediate action or administration.
definitions.technical: An urgent timing directive rather than a repeating frequency schedule.

examples: STAT indicates urgency but does not supply a dose or route.

definitions.simple: Two times in one day, according to the stated schedule.
definitions.standard: A frequency instruction indicating two administrations per day; exact timing should be confirmed.
definitions.technical: A dosing-frequency expression that requires explicit timing and interval details in the complete instruction.

examples: BID or BD can indicate twice daily; use the complete labeled schedule.

definitions.simple: Three times in one day, according to the stated schedule.
definitions.standard: A frequency instruction indicating three administrations per day; exact timing should be confirmed.
definitions.technical: A dosing-frequency expression that requires explicit timing and interval details in the complete instruction.

examples: TID is an abbreviation for three times daily; use the complete labeled schedule.

definitions.simple: Four times in one day, according to the stated schedule.
definitions.standard: A frequency instruction indicating four administrations per day; exact timing should be confirmed.
definitions.technical: A dosing-frequency expression that requires explicit timing and interval details in the complete instruction.

examples: QID is an abbreviation for four times daily; use the complete labeled schedule.

lessons.title: Introduction to medical word parts
lessons.description: Learn how prefixes, roots, and suffixes help explain the structure of medical words.
objectives: Separate morphology from a trusted medical definition

sections.title: Three kinds of word parts
sections.content: A prefix often changes position, amount, or speed. A root usually names a body structure or core idea. A suffix often describes a condition, procedure, or specialty.

sections.title: Use word parts carefully
sections.content: Word parts explain structure, but they do not establish a diagnosis or replace a reviewed definition. Unknown fragments should remain unknown.

sections.title: Example: tachycardia
sections.content: tachy means fast, cardi refers to the heart, and -ia means a condition or state. The reviewed definition still provides the complete meaning.

lessons.title: Cardiovascular terminology basics
lessons.description: Explore a small set of heart and blood-pressure terms and their relationships.

sections.title: Blood pressure language
sections.content: Hypertension refers to sustained high blood pressure. Hypotension refers to blood pressure that is lower than expected. Neither word alone states the cause.

sections.title: Heart-rate language
sections.content: tachy- means fast and brady- means slow. When combined with cardi and -ia, they form tachycardia and bradycardia.

quiz_questions.prompt: What does the suffix -itis usually indicate?
quiz_questions.explanation: The suffix -itis indicates inflammation involving the named structure.

quiz_questions.prompt: In tachycardia, what does tachy- mean?
quiz_questions.explanation: tachy- indicates fast or rapid activity.

quiz_questions.prompt: Which medical term matches the phrase high blood pressure?
quiz_questions.explanation: Hypertension is the medical term for persistently elevated blood pressure.

quiz_questions.prompt: What is the safest interpretation of MS without context?
quiz_questions.explanation: MS is context-dependent and can have multiple medical meanings.

options.text: It has multiple possible meanings; ask for context
